The generated narrative/spec pages for TriggerDefinition and SubscriptionTopic were not reviewed; they could clarify the semantics of `subscriptionTopic` exclusivity and condition-without-data use.
The trigger-type ValueSets did not include expansion entries. The comparison used the complete CodeSystem concepts instead.

scope.scopeNotesMd: This report compares the local R4 and R6 core StructureDefinitions for the assigned datatype `TriggerDefinition`, plus the directly bound trigger-type ValueSet/CodeSystem. Findings are limited to local TriggerDefinition element, type, terminology, and invariant changes. Inherited Element/DataType details are deliberately excluded under the assignment rule.
outOfScope: Inherited Element changes such as `id`, `extension`, `ele-1`, and extension governance text are excluded from findings.
The R4-to-R6 baseDefinition shift from Element to DataType is a global datatype hierarchy issue and is not counted as a local TriggerDefinition finding.
Internal semantics of the R6 SubscriptionTopic resource are out of scope except where TriggerDefinition directly references it.
Dependent resource/profile changes in PlanDefinition, EventDefinition, Task, Claim, ClaimResponse, ExplanationOfBenefit, and extensions using TriggerDefinition are out of scope.
Package-wide JSON schema/OpenAPI generation differences are out of scope except for serialization consequences directly implied by TriggerDefinition element changes.

narrativeReportMd:
# TriggerDefinition R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
A local hard R4-to-R6 validation break was found: `TriggerDefinition.timing[x]` no longer accepts `Reference(Schedule)`. R6 also adds a SubscriptionTopic trigger form and code-based named-event support, which are mostly R6-to-R4 representability and runtime-dispatch risks rather than old-instance breaks.

## Scope
The analysis used the R4 and R6 core `StructureDefinition-TriggerDefinition.json` files, package metadata/indexes, and the local trigger-type ValueSet/CodeSystem files. Inherited Element/DataType changes, including the R6 baseDefinition shift through `DataType`, are out of scope for local findings.

## Main migration themes
The main forward migration task is replacing any R4 `timingReference` values with inline or primitive timing. The main reverse/cross-version task is preserving R6-only trigger forms: `type = subscription-topic`, `subscriptionTopic`, and code-only named events. Validator behavior also changes because R6 removes the old rule that `condition` requires `data`.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest direct break is `TriggerDefinition.timing[x]` type narrowing. The highest R6-to-R4 risks are the new `subscription-topic` code and `subscriptionTopic` canonical element.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most useful for the intended semantics of `subscriptionTopic` exclusivity and the rationale for allowing `condition` without `data`, because those points are visible in the computable definitions but would benefit from official narrative or committee notes.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several R6 changes could have been made less disruptive by retaining old choices/invariants or using extensions, but that would reduce first-class R6 validation and tooling support for SubscriptionTopic and coded triggers.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze the base `DataType` hierarchy shift separately, and review `SubscriptionTopic` plus any official cross-version ConceptMaps before implementing automated R6-to-R4 conversion.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `TriggerDefinition` has one clear local hard break: R4 `timingReference` to `Schedule` is no longer allowed. R6 also adds SubscriptionTopic and coded named-event forms that are not cleanly R4-representable. Confidence is high for the computable deltas, with remaining uncertainty around official rationale and narrative semantics.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Forward migration should focus on choice-type narrowing for `timing[x]`. Cross-version conversion should treat `subscription-topic`, `subscriptionTopic`, and code-only named events as semantic data that cannot be dropped without loss. Runtime consumers should update trigger dispatch logic and validation rules for the changed invariants.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high because the local R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions directly expose the changed element lists, choice types, bindings, and constraints, and the trigger-type CodeSystems are complete. Confidence is lower for design justification and prevalence because no official diff, narrative page review, terminology expansion, or authoritative ConceptMap was available.

findings.title: TriggerDefinition.timing[x] no longer permits Reference(Schedule)

oldState.summary: 0..1 timing choice allowed Timing, Reference(Schedule), date, or dateTime.

semanticText.definition: The timing of the event (if this is a periodic trigger).

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, periodic trigger timing could be supplied inline as `Timing`, as a primitive `date`/`dateTime`, or indirectly with `timingReference` pointing at a `Schedule`.

newState.summary: 0..1 timing choice allows Timing, date, or dateTime; Reference(Schedule) is absent.

semanticText.definition: The timing of the event (if this is a periodic trigger).

newState.narrativeMd: R6 removes the reference choice, so the JSON/XML choice name `timingReference` is no longer valid for `TriggerDefinition`.

facts.note: The removed type was `Reference` constrained to `Schedule`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct type-domain narrowing on a choice element. An R4 instance with `timingReference` can satisfy R4 validation but fail R6 validation because R6 has no `Reference` choice for this path. Generated R6 models and serializers are also unlikely to expose a `timingReference` property.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk is primarily migration/runtime correctness. A lost schedule reference could change when a trigger fires, but the supplied package inputs do not show common example use.

justification.inferredGoal: Prefer self-contained or primitive timing for trigger definitions rather than referencing a Schedule resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `Reference(Schedule)` as a deprecated or discouraged `timing[x]` choice while allowing R6 authors to prefer inline `Timing`, `date`, or `dateTime`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Removing the choice creates the only direct old-valid/new-invalid TriggerDefinition break. The apparent goal of simpler, self-contained timing is reasonable, but the local evidence does not show that Schedule references had to be invalid in base R6. Because retaining the existing choice would preserve all R4 `timingReference` instances with manageable implementation cost, the hard break looks probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could keep `Reference(Schedule)` in `TriggerDefinition.timing[x]`, mark it deprecated or discouraged, and use profiles or guidance to prefer inline `Timing`, `date`, or `dateTime`. The tradeoff is that generic R6 tooling would still need to understand and resolve Schedule references, and deprecated timing representations can linger indefinitely, but this is a moderate compatibility cost rather than evidence that removal was necessary.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances but leaves R6 consumers with an older indirect timing representation that may persist and require Schedule resolution.

evidence.detail: R4 lists Timing, Reference(targetProfile Schedule), date, and dateTime.
R6 lists Timing, date, and dateTime only.

examples.examplesMd: The examples are TriggerDefinition fragments. The migration example is only lossless if the referenced `Schedule` can be deterministically converted to inline `Timing`.

findings.narrativeMd: `TriggerDefinition.timing[x]` is the one clear R4-to-R6 hard instance break found locally. R4 allowed periodic trigger timing to be represented as a reference to a `Schedule`; R6 removes that choice. Existing R4 payloads, generated classes, FHIRPath expressions, or transforms that use `timingReference` need explicit migration rather than simple revalidation under R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 fragment such as `type: periodic` plus `timingReference` can be valid in R4 and invalid in R6 because R6 no longer defines the `Reference` choice at this path. The reverse direction is not problematic for this specific narrowing: any R6 `timingTiming`, `timingDate`, or `timingDateTime` value uses a type that R4 also allowed.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Search for `timingReference` on TriggerDefinition values. Where the referenced `Schedule` is resolvable and simple enough, convert it to `timingTiming`; where it is not, preserve the reference with an extension, a cross-version profile, or manual review. Tests should include `timingReference`, `timingTiming`, `timingDate`, and `timingDateTime` cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The same modeling goal could probably have been achieved by retaining `Reference(Schedule)` and marking it discouraged or profile-restricted. Removing the choice simplifies R6 consumers but forces legacy data transformation and may be lossy when a Schedule cannot be flattened.

findings.title: Required trigger-type binding adds the `subscription-topic` code

oldState.summary: Required binding to trigger-type version 4.0.1 without `subscription-topic`.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 ValueSet composes the complete `http://hl7.org/fhir/trigger-type` CodeSystem; no expansion resource was present in the package. Recursive CodeSystem concepts were compared instead.

semanticText.short: named-event | periodic | data-changed | data-added | data-modified | data-removed | data-accessed | data-access-ended

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed named, periodic, data, and access trigger types. Because the binding is required, codes outside that set are invalid in R4.

newState.summary: Required binding to trigger-type version 6.0.0-ballot4 including new `subscription-topic`.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The new code is present in the R6 complete CodeSystem and appears in the R6 TriggerDefinition.type short description.

semanticText.short: named-event | periodic | data-changed | data-added | data-modified | data-removed | data-accessed | data-access-ended | subscription-topic

newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds `subscription-topic` as a first-class trigger type. The root invariant also gives that code special validation behavior by requiring `subscriptionTopic`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 codes remain present in R6, so this does not invalidate old R4 instances. The new required-bound code creates a significant reverse-direction risk: an R6 instance with `type = subscription-topic` is invalid against R4 terminology and will also surprise enum-based code compiled from R4 definitions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrectly downgrading a subscription-topic trigger to a generic named event could change event routing or subscription semantics.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent triggers defined by the R6 SubscriptionTopic resource directly in TriggerDefinition.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: adding `subscription-topic` widens the required value set and does not invalidate any R4 trigger-type code.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The new code aligns with first-class SubscriptionTopic support and preserves the R4 code set. Since no R4-valid instance becomes invalid, the breakage is limited to R6-to-R4 conversion and runtime consumers that assume the R4 enum is closed. The named-event or extension approach is a down-conversion mitigation, not a backward-compatible alternative for an R4-to-R6 break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because this is a terminology widening. R6 could have avoided reverse incompatibility by overloading `named-event` or an extension, but that would obscure the SubscriptionTopic semantics and is outside the calibrated backward-compatible-alternative category.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The cost is reverse-direction enum and validator handling for R6 data, not an avoidable R4-to-R6 base break.

evidence.detail: R4 binding is required to trigger-type|4.0.1.
R6 binding is required to trigger-type|6.0.0-ballot4 and the short description includes `subscription-topic`.
R6 CodeSystem adds `subscription-topic` with definition `The trigger occurs as defined by a subscription topic.`

examples.examplesMd: The fragment uses an R6-only trigger type. R4 has no allowed `type` code with the same required-binding meaning.

findings.narrativeMd: `TriggerDefinition.type` remains mandatory and required-bound, but R6 expands the allowed code set with `subscription-topic`. This is not an old-data validation break because R4's existing codes were retained. It is a high-value migration finding because R4 code generators often model required code bindings as closed enums, and R4 validators will reject the new code.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid `type` codes remain R6-valid. However, a valid R6 `subscription-topic` trigger is not valid R4 because the required R4 ValueSet does not include the code. Runtime systems that use exhaustive switches over R4 trigger types need a new branch or a safe unknown-code path before processing R6 data.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4 conversion, do not silently coerce `subscription-topic` to another code unless a domain-specific rule says that semantic loss is acceptable. Prefer a cross-version extension or reject/queue such instances for manual policy handling. Update generated enums and trigger dispatch tests to include the new code.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 model could have avoided a new required-bound code by carrying the SubscriptionTopic canonical in an extension while keeping `type = named-event`. That would preserve R4 validation but lose clear R6 semantics and machine validation. The added code is therefore probably justified but not backward-compatible.

findings.title: R6 adds TriggerDefinition.subscriptionTopic as a canonical reference to SubscriptionTopic

oldState.summary: No `subscriptionTopic` element existed in R4 TriggerDefinition.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could not carry a base `TriggerDefinition.subscriptionTopic` property. Implementations would need an extension or a different trigger representation.

newState.summary: Optional 0..1 canonical element targeting SubscriptionTopic, marked summary.

semanticText.definition: A reference to a SubscriptionTopic resource that defines the event. If this element is provided, no other information about the trigger definition may be supplied.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 introduces a first-class canonical pointer to a `SubscriptionTopic`. Its definition also says that when this element is present, no other trigger-definition information may be supplied.

facts.newValue: If this element is provided, no other information about the trigger definition may be supplied.
facts.note: This exclusivity text was observed in ElementDefinition.definition; no separate invariant enforcing all such exclusions was found on TriggerDefinition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional element additions do not break old R4 instances moving to R6. They do create reverse-direction and parser risks: R4 parsers/validators do not know the base element, and the target resource `SubscriptionTopic` is outside this datatype's R4 shape.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: If subscription-topic triggers drive event routing, dropping the canonical can materially change behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow TriggerDefinition to delegate event semantics to the SubscriptionTopic resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: `subscriptionTopic` is optional additive R6 content, so existing R4 TriggerDefinition instances can still validate in R6 without it.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: A first-class canonical link to SubscriptionTopic is coherent with the new trigger type. It creates reverse-direction representability work, but an optional added element does not invalidate R4 data. Extension or backport strategies are mitigations for older R4 systems, not less-breaking base R6 alternatives.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible alternative applies under the calibration rule because the finding is additive optional R6 content. Representing the canonical only as an extension would help R4 receivers but would weaken R6 discoverability, validation, and code generation rather than avoid an old-instance break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 conversion needs extension or sidecar preservation, but the optional base element is not an R4-to-R6 break.

evidence.detail: R4 local element list has no `TriggerDefinition.subscriptionTopic`.
R6 adds 0..1 canonical targeting SubscriptionTopic and marks it summary.
evidence.quote: A reference to a SubscriptionTopic resource that defines the event.

examples.examplesMd: The base R4 datatype cannot carry `subscriptionTopic` without an extension or out-of-band mapping.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds `subscriptionTopic`, a new optional canonical element. Optional additions are forward-compatible for existing R4 content, but this one is structurally important because it introduces a new first-class representation for a trigger whose semantics live in `SubscriptionTopic`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is not broken by the added optional element. R6-to-R4 conversion is not clean: an R4 validator will reject the unknown `subscriptionTopic` property, and removing it would discard the event definition. The additional prose rule saying no other trigger information may be supplied with `subscriptionTopic` may not be fully enforced unless implementations check it explicitly.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When down-converting, preserve the canonical in an extension or a sidecar mapping rather than dropping it. When validating R6, add tests for `subscriptionTopic` alone and with other trigger details, because the exclusivity sentence may require business-rule enforcement beyond the listed invariants.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The first-class element is useful for R6 but could have been delivered as an extension for R4 compatibility. That alternative would avoid unknown base elements in R4 but would make the new feature less visible to generic R6 tooling.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is useful to decide how strictly to enforce the definition sentence `If this element is provided, no other information about the trigger definition may be supplied`, because the local invariant list only requires `subscriptionTopic` when `type = subscription-topic`.

findings.title: Named-event triggers may now use CodeableConcept code instead of name

oldState.summary: R4 had no `code` element and invariant trd-3 required `name` when `type = named-event`.

constraints.human: A named event requires a name, a periodic event requires timing, and a data event requires data
constraints.expression: (type = 'named-event' implies name.exists()) and (type = 'periodic' implies timing.exists()) and (type.startsWith('data-') implies data.exists())

semanticText.comment: Named events are completely pre-coordinated, and no other information can be specified for the event.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, a named event was identified through the string `name`; a named-event trigger without `name` failed the local `trd-3` invariant.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional `code` and changes trd-3 so `type = named-event` requires `name` or `code`.

constraints.human: A named event requires a name or code, a periodic event requires timing, a data event requires data, and a subscription topic requires a reference to a subscription topic
constraints.expression: (type = 'named-event' implies (name.exists() or code.exists())) and (type = 'periodic' implies timing.exists()) and (type.startsWith('data-') implies data.exists()) and (type = 'subscription-topic' implies subscriptionTopic.exists())

semanticText.comment: Named events remain described as pre-coordinated in the root comment; R6 also has `TriggerDefinition.code` with definition `A code that identifies the event.`

newState.narrativeMd: R6 allows a coded named event by adding `TriggerDefinition.code` (`CodeableConcept`) and relaxing the named-event part of `trd-3` from `name.exists()` to `name.exists() or code.exists()`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same root invariant key `trd-3` exists in both versions and continues to encode type-specific required companion elements.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a constraint weakening plus an optional element addition. It does not make old R4 named events invalid, but it permits R6 named events that R4 cannot validate because `name` is absent and `code` is unknown. Runtime code that looks only at `name` for named-event dispatch may miss valid R6 triggers.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Named events are often used for workflow or CDS trigger dispatch; failing to recognize a code-only named event could suppress expected behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow named events to be identified by a coded concept rather than only by a string/URI name.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: adding optional `code` and weakening `trd-3` preserves R4-valid named events; the issue is R6-to-R4 code-only events.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal to support coded event identity is reasonable, and all R4 named-event instances with `name` remain valid. The prior alternative of adding `code` while keeping `name` mandatory is a reverse-compatibility compromise, not a needed base-design alternative for R4-to-R6 compatibility, and it would fail the code-only use case.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No R4-to-R6 backward-compatible alternative is applicable because the base rule is weakened. Down-converters may derive `name` from `code` or use an extension, but those are migration mitigations for R6-only instances, not evidence that R6 should keep the R4 invariant.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4-era dispatch and conversion must handle code-only named events, but keeping `name` mandatory would block part of the R6 expressiveness rather than avoid an R4-to-R6 break.

evidence.detail: R6 named-event branch requires `name.exists() or code.exists()`.
R6 adds optional CodeableConcept `code` with definition `A code that identifies the event.`

examples.examplesMd: A code-only named event is valid under the R6 invariant but would fail R4 both because `code` is unknown and because `name` is absent. Mapping a coding to `name` requires local policy and may be lossy.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 changes the named-event representation from name-only to name-or-code. This is useful for terminology-based triggers, but it changes a validation assumption that R4 consumers could rely on: a named event no longer necessarily has `name` populated.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4 instance becomes invalid merely because of this change. A valid R6 code-only named event is not R4-representable without deriving a `name` or using an extension. Strict generated R4 parsers will also reject the `code` property.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update trigger dispatch logic to check `code` as well as `name`. For R6-to-R4 conversion, define a deterministic mapping from selected codings to `name` only where governance exists; otherwise preserve the CodeableConcept in an extension and flag the instance for review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping `name` mandatory while adding optional `code` would have been more backward-compatible and would still support coded metadata. The tradeoff is that some R6 authors would need to provide a redundant string identifier when the code is already authoritative.

findings.title: R6 removes the invariant that condition requires data

oldState.summary: R4 invariant trd-2 required `condition` only when `data` exists.

constraints.human: A condition only if there is a data requirement

semanticText.comment: For data events, the data element specifies the structured component, and the condition element provides additional optional refinement.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 tied `condition` to data triggers: a TriggerDefinition with `condition` but no `data` failed `trd-2`.

newState.summary: No `trd-2` invariant is present; `condition` remains optional 0..1 Expression.

semanticText.comment: The root comment still describes condition as additional optional refinement of the data component, but the computable invariant no longer restricts it to data triggers.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 removes the computable condition-implies-data rule. A condition can now appear on a periodic or named trigger without a data requirement, subject to the other remaining invariants.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R4 root constraint key `trd-2` has no corresponding R6 root constraint; `trd-1` and `trd-3` remain present.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Removing an error invariant is not an R4-to-R6 validation break. It does allow R6 instances that fail R4 validation and may affect business logic that assumed conditions only refine data requirements.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: A condition on a periodic or named trigger could change when a trigger fires. Misinterpreting or dropping it during conversion could alter workflow behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Permit conditional gating of non-data triggers such as periodic or named events.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: removing `trd-2` weakens validation and preserves R4-valid instances; only R6 condition-without-data instances have R4 representability issues.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 `condition` comment explicitly says the element can be specified for any trigger type, so the invariant removal appears to be an intentional broadening rather than an unexplained inconsistency. Keeping `trd-2` would preserve an R4 assumption but would defeat the R6 goal of conditional gating for periodic, named, or subscription-topic triggers.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible alternative applies for R4-to-R6 compatibility because a less restrictive invariant cannot invalidate R4-conformant data. Profiles or conversion rules can reject or preserve R6 condition-without-data cases for R4 systems, but those are reverse-direction mitigations rather than base R6 alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 validators and trigger evaluators may need new policy for conditions on non-data triggers, but there is no old-instance validation break to avoid.

evidence.detail: R4 has an error invariant requiring condition only if data exists.
R6 root constraints include `trd-1` and `trd-3`, but no `trd-2`.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is valid with respect to the changed local TriggerDefinition invariants in R6 but would violate R4 `trd-2` because it has `condition` without `data`.

findings.narrativeMd: The R4 invariant `trd-2` was a local conformance rule tying `condition` to `data`. R6 removes that rule, so condition can be used more broadly. This is not an old-data break, but it is material for validators, trigger evaluators, and down-conversion logic.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances remain valid with respect to this rule because R6 is less restrictive. R6 instances with `condition` and no `data` are not R4-valid. Runtime code that evaluates conditions only in a data-trigger context needs to be updated or it may ignore valid R6 conditions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6 consumers, test condition evaluation on named and periodic triggers, not only data triggers. For R6-to-R4 conversion, either reject condition-without-data instances, preserve the condition in an extension, or apply a domain-specific transformation that introduces an appropriate data requirement if one exists.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The base change could have been avoided by preserving `trd-2` and adding an extension/profile for non-data trigger conditions. That would protect R4 assumptions but would make the broadened R6 use case less interoperable in the base datatype.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review the R6 narrative/spec page or committee notes if available; the computable definition removes the rule, but the retained comment still describes `condition` primarily as data-trigger refinement.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, and abstract flag continue to identify the same datatype. The baseDefinition shift is noted as inherited/global and excluded from findings.
Existing local element cardinalities for `type`, `name`, `timing[x]`, `data`, and `condition` are unchanged. Newly added `code` and `subscriptionTopic` are optional 0..1.
No local TriggerDefinition element became a modifier; changed and added local elements have `isModifier = false`.
No slicing definitions were found on local TriggerDefinition elements in either version.
No fixed, pattern, or default value constraints were found on local TriggerDefinition elements in either version.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex constraints were found on TriggerDefinition elements.
Existing local summary flags remained stable. The new R6 `code` and `subscriptionTopic` elements are summary elements, which is noted in the relevant findings but is not itself an old-instance break.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Artifact maturity/status metadata does not change instance validation for TriggerDefinition content by itself.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance and dependency policies may treat the R6 datatype as more stable because status is now `active` and `experimental` is explicitly false.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds jurisdiction metadata and updates publisher/contact information
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: These are definitional metadata changes, not instance-shape or validation changes for TriggerDefinition values.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Metadata-sensitive package comparison tools may report these differences, but they should not be triaged as instance-breaking changes.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 changes TriggerDefinition's baseDefinition from `Element` to `DataType`. Per scope rules, that inherited/global datatype hierarchy issue should be assessed in the base `DataType` report rather than as a local TriggerDefinition finding.
R6 `TriggerDefinition.subscriptionTopic` canonically targets `SubscriptionTopic`; safe migration requires understanding that resource's own R4/R6 availability and breaking changes.
No authoritative mapping was available for converting `subscription-topic`, `subscriptionTopic`, or code-only named events into R4-compatible TriggerDefinition content.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff or change proposal was available in the local inputs, so justification and avoidability assessments are inferred from the computable definitions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official FHIR change notes, ballot reconciliation, or generated diff pages for TriggerDefinition.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The trigger-type ValueSet files did not include expansions. The comparison used the complete trigger-type CodeSystem hierarchy, which is adequate for identifying the added code but not a formal expansion comparison.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run terminology expansion for both ValueSet versions with the official FHIR terminology server or package terminology tooling.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Generated narrative/spec pages were not reviewed. They may clarify whether `subscriptionTopic` exclusivity is intended to be validator-enforced and why `condition` was decoupled from `data`.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Inspect the R6 ballot narrative pages for TriggerDefinition, SubscriptionTopic, and any linked change notes.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The report did not comprehensively analyze real-world implementation guides or production examples, so expected prevalence is mostly unknown or inferred as rare from local package examples.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Search implementation guides and deployed artifacts for `timingReference`, code-only named events, condition-without-data patterns, and SubscriptionTopic trigger usage.

crossArtifactPatternsToCheck: Datatypes that removed Reference choices from timing[x] elements
Required-bound code systems with R6-only codes
